# Command line

The `mallet` command. This page shows the output of `--help` for the command and each of its subcommands.

## mallet

```text
Diagnoses a modded game setup and explains what is wrong

Usage: mallet [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>

Commands:
  scan     Examine the setup and print what is wrong with it
  report   Print the result of the last scan again without scanning
  explain  Explain a kind of finding: what it means and what to do about it
  kinds    List every kind of finding Mod Mallet can report
  vortex   Have Vortex act on a finding, through a small Vortex extension
  help     Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
      --lang <LANG>
          Language of the output: `en` or `de`

          [default: en]

  -v, --verbose
          Show which places were read and how they were found, list the notes, and print what Mod Mallet is doing to the error stream

  -h, --help
          Print help

  -V, --version
          Print version
```

## mallet scan

```text
Examine the setup and print what is wrong with it.

A scan only reads. It changes nothing in the game, the mods or the mod manager.

Usage: mallet scan [OPTIONS]

Options:
      --game-dir <DIR>
          The directory the game is installed in. Detected if omitted

      --lang <LANG>
          Language of the output: `en` or `de`

          [default: en]

      --local-dir <DIR>
          The directory that holds `plugins.txt`, the game's list of active plugins. Detected if omitted

  -v, --verbose
          Show which places were read and how they were found, list the notes, and print what Mod Mallet is doing to the error stream

      --extender-log <FILE>
          The script extender's log file. Detected if omitted

      --deployment-manifest <FILE>
          The Vortex deployment manifest. Detected if omitted

      --manager-state <FILE>
          The backup of Vortex's state. Detected if omitted

      --downloads-dir <DIR>
          The directory Vortex keeps downloaded mod archives in. Detected if omitted

      --unpacker <FILE>
          The 7-Zip program used to look into mod archives. Detected if omitted

      --no-cache
          Do not use the cache: read everything again, and do not remember the result for `mallet report`

      --format <FORMAT>
          How to print the result

          Possible values:
          - text: Sentences for people
          - json: The scan report as JSON, described by `schemas/scan-report.schema.json`

          [default: text]

      --notes
          Also list the notes: things worth knowing that need no action. The JSON format always contains them

      --cache <FILE>
          Where the result of the last scan is kept

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

  -V, --version
          Print version
```

## mallet vortex

```text
Have Vortex act on a finding, through a small Vortex extension.

Mod Mallet does not change mods itself. It asks Vortex, which does what its own menu entry would do.

Usage: mallet vortex [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>

Commands:
  status             Say whether the extension is installed and Vortex is answering
  install-extension  Put the extension into Vortex's plugin folder. Vortex loads it the next time it starts
  reinstall          Ask Vortex to run a mod's installer again
  help               Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
      --lang <LANG>
          Language of the output: `en` or `de`

          [default: en]

      --vortex-data-dir <DIR>
          The directory in which Vortex keeps its data. Detected if omitted

      --link-dir <DIR>
          The folder shared with the Vortex extension. Detected if omitted

  -v, --verbose
          Show which places were read and how they were found, list the notes, and print what Mod Mallet is doing to the error stream

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

  -V, --version
          Print version
```
